claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS, and multi-cloud with CDK was nearly impossible.
SST was originally built on top of AWS CDK, which let developers define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.

AWS CDK is AWS-only, supports only TypeScript and Python, has slower deployment due to CloudFormation, and AWS Secrets Manager only for secrets; Pulumi supports any programming language, faster direct execution, and cross-cloud secrets.
AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python.
AWS CDK secrets management is limited to AWS Secrets Manager only.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK deployments.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C#.
Pulumi has built-in extensibility features such as custom providers and dynamic components.
Ion is the code name for a new SST engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and also bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
A Founding Engineer at SST said that with Pulumi the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code and can handle advanced things traditional IaC tools can't.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS simplifies day one tasks, documented in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
Pulumi Insights product page describes improved visibility and debugging capabilities.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make the underlying cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud dependency; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account rather than in Pulumi Cloud.
SST v3 is the Ion-based rewrite of SST.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure and code in a single `sst.config.ts` file using SST components.
Through 2023, SST's provisioning layer was built directly on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion; Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN)."

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources."
SST docs 'What is SST' say: "SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi."
Gautier Blandin's article 'Terraform, Pulumi, SST: a tradeoff analysis' says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: "You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now."
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi plus Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and others, and a Pulumiverse Vercel provider.

platform/package.json in anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst) lists @pulumi/pulumi, @pulumi/aws, @pulumi/cloudflare, @pulumi/command, @pulumi/docker-build, @pulumi/random, @pulumi/tls, and @pulumiverse/vercel as direct dependencies.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
Pulumi users can consume Terraform providers directly via the provider bridge.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state that "all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments", with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider is described as taking "a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`"; Defang deploys Docker Compose applications to the cloud.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads a week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode now has a larger GitHub following (stars) than SST itself.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The team's attention on opencode hasn't changed SST's release cadence.
Pulumi Cloud provides cross-team visibility into infrastructure state; policy as code enables central guardrails; components enable sharing infrastructure patterns across an organization.
Pulumi's engine provides dependency resolution, preview and diff, state tracking, and plumbing to hundreds of provider APIs.
SST's repository is anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
